Definition: apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively):--gate.
BiblicalUsage: Pyle means a gate, the leaf of a folding entrance. Jesus says, Enter ye in at the strait gate, for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life. He says the gates of hell shall not prevail against His church. And Jesus suffered without the gate, that He might sanctify the people with His own blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gate is the decision of my life: there are two gates, and I must enter the strait one, because the wide one leads to destruction. I hold that the gates of hell cannot prevail against the church, because the One who suffered outside the gate now stands inside it with His people.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
